AgentStep.description:
The agent steps a turn can report, in the UI's catalogue (docs/design/system.md §8).

``plan``, ``search``, ``rank`` and ``triggers`` are recall's (S3); ``fetch`` (S4) is
reserved: in the schema so the UI's catalogue is complete, not emitted yet.
AgentStep.title: AgentStep

AggregateTrace.description: An exact number from SQL, with the ids it counted (S3.5).
AggregateTrace.title: AggregateTrace

CitationsEvent.description:
The ``[n]`` markers of the reply, mapped by code to memories or past turns (S3.8).
A marker that matched no evidence was stripped from the reply and is counted here.
CitationsEvent.title: CitationsEvent

Classification.description: What one proposed memory was taken to be.
Classification.title: Classification

CountCheck.description: Soft-channel hits that look like what was counted but weren't (S3.6).
CountCheck.title: CountCheck

model.description: A picker model (`id` from `/v1/meta` `picker.choices`) for every chat step of this turn. Omitted: the configured per-step routing.
model.title: Model

DecisionEvent.description: Decision panel: kinds, date and entity resolutions, reconciliation, rationale.
DecisionEvent.title: DecisionEvent

DevLoginIn.description: Optional: log in as another dev user (dev auth only), e.g. a fresh one per E2E test.
DevLoginIn.title: DevLoginIn

EntityResolution.description: How a mention ("my wife", "Severance") was matched to an entity, or why one was made.
EntityResolution.title: EntityResolution

EntityTrace.description: How a mention in the question was resolved, including relation paths followed.
EntityTrace.title: EntityTrace

message.description: Human-readable, safe to show to users.
message.title: Message

ErrorEvent.description: A turn-ending or step-level error, with a stable code and a user-safe message.
ErrorEvent.title: ErrorEvent

FallbackInfo.description: Set on a model call that was served by the step's fallback model (FR-14.4).
FallbackInfo.title: FallbackInfo

FoundBy.description: One channel that found a candidate, and the candidate's rank in it (1 = top).
FoundBy.title: FoundBy

HeldWriteOut.description: A write the policy held for confirmation (S2.3).
HeldWriteOut.title: HeldWriteOut

IntentEvent.description: What the agent decided the message is (FR-1.2).
IntentEvent.title: IntentEvent

ItemDetailOut.description: A plain view of one memory item, its entity roles, links and triggers (S2.11).
ItemDetailOut.title: ItemDetailOut

ItemEditIn.description: A glass-box edit of one memory (S3.12). Only the fields given change.

date_expression.description: Free text read by the resolver: 'Friday'.
date_expression.title: Date Expression

ItemEditIn.title: ItemEditIn

ItemStatus.description: About the record ("deleted"), not the world (that is ``state``).
ItemStatus.title: ItemStatus

Kind.description: What a memory is, defined by how it behaves over time.
Kind.title: Kind

MemoryDiffEvent.description: Memory diff panel, built from the write log so it can't disagree with what happened.
MemoryDiffEvent.title: MemoryDiffEvent

picker.description: Null when no picker is configured.

ModelCallEvent.description: One model call: who served it, what it cost, how long it took (FR-14.8, FR-19.2).

cache_hits.description: Embeddings reused from the content-hash cache (FR-14.6).
cache_hits.title: Cache Hits

ModelCallEvent.title: ModelCallEvent

available.description: False when it can't be used (live mode, no key).
available.title: Available

id.description: provider:model, as sent in a turn's `model`.
id.title: Id

simulated.description: The fake provider stands in for it (no credentials).
simulated.title: Simulated

weight.description: Quota tokens per token on this model, against the baseline (1 = baseline).
weight.title: Weight

Normalisation.description: A slug the model proposed, and what normalisation chose (reuse beats invention).
Normalisation.title: Normalisation

PickerOut.description: The model picker (ADR-0030): choices in display order, grouped by provider.
PickerOut.title: PickerOut

PolicyEvent.description: A write-policy decision on one proposed operation (FR-4.6).
PolicyEvent.title: PolicyEvent

ReconcileInfo.description: How a proposed memory relates to what is stored (S2.8).
ReconcileInfo.title: ReconcileInfo

RelaxStep.description: One loosening of the filters after every filtered channel came back empty (S3.6).
RelaxStep.title: RelaxStep

RetrievalCandidate.description: A memory (or, for conversation recall, a past turn) that reached fusion.

matched_key.description: The key kind the search matched on ('matched via cue key').

soft_only.description: Found by the soft channel only.
soft_only.title: Soft Only

RetrievalCandidate.title: RetrievalCandidate

RetrievalEvent.description:
Retrieval panel: the plan, what each tool and the soft channel found, fusion, relaxation,
rerank and what reached the answer (S3.13).
RetrievalEvent.title: RetrievalEvent

Shape.description: What kind of question a sub-query is (S3.4). Code maps each shape to its tools.
Shape.title: Shape

SseStepStarted.description: An agent step began (ADR-0029). Its ``step`` event follows in a ``turn.event`` frame.
SseStepStarted.title: SseStepStarted

quota.description: The user's quota after this turn (null if it can't be read).

SseTurnEvent.description: A turn event, as it was persisted (the same ``seq`` and body as ``/events``).
SseTurnEvent.title: SseTurnEvent

quota.description: The user's quota after this turn (null if it can't be read).

StepEvent.description: One agent step that ran: how it ended and how long it took (ADR-0029).
StepEvent.title: StepEvent

StepModel.description: Which provider and model served a step, and with which prompt version (FR-19.2).
StepModel.title: StepModel

SubQueryTrace.description: One part of the plan, what ran for it, and what it found.
SubQueryTrace.title: SubQueryTrace

TimeClock.description:
Which clock a time expression sets: when it happened, when it was true, when it is due,
or when to remind. Recall also filters on when something was mentioned (said or saved).
TimeClock.title: TimeClock

TimeResolution.description: One time expression, resolved by code (never the model): expression -> value.

anchor.description: Recall: the event a window was computed from ('Goa trip').
anchor.title: Anchor

item_id.description: The memory this date was written to (for a one-tap fix).
item_id.title: Item Id

TimeResolution.title: TimeResolution

TimingSpan.description: A non-model span for the waterfall (fusion, selection).
TimingSpan.title: TimingSpan

ToolCallEvent.description:
Tool calls panel: tool, summarised arguments and result, policy verdict. Retrieval tools
are ``read`` (no write policy applies); memory writer ops are ``write``.
ToolCallEvent.title: ToolCallEvent

ToolRun.description: One retrieval tool call of a sub-query.
ToolRun.title: ToolRun

url.description: Link to the raw trace; null when unavailable or disabled.
url.title: Url

TraceStatus.description: Whether the turn's trace reached the trace backend (FR-9.2).
TraceStatus.title: TraceStatus

TurnKind.description:
What started a turn: a message, an undo, a confirmation of a held write, an edit from the
glass box or Upcoming, or the system (background jobs). Every kind is stored, auditable and
undoable the same way.
TurnKind.title: TurnKind

kind.description: user (a message), undo, confirm (a held write) or system (a background job).

parent_turn_id.description: The undone turn, or the turn whose held write was confirmed.
parent_turn_id.title: Parent Turn Id

next_before.description: Pass as `before` to get the next (older) page.
next_before.title: Next Before

TurnStreamFrame.description: One server-sent event on the turn stream: `event:` name, `data:` JSON.
TurnStreamFrame.title: TurnStreamFrame

day.description: The local date, YYYY-MM-DD, in the workspace timezone.
day.title: Day

via.description: occurred, routine, due or trigger (a reminder)
via.title: Via

note.description: The due-soon note for the chat, built in code.
note.title: Note

Usage.description:
Usage of one model call.

``input_tokens`` counts *uncached* input only; cached reads are in ``cached_input_tokens``.
Adapters normalise to this split so cost is always
``input * p_in + cached * p_cached + output * p_out`` from the price table.

charged_tokens.description: Quota tokens: all tokens at the model's weight against the baseline. Null on calls recorded before quota was weighted (they count as total tokens).
charged_tokens.title: Charged Tokens

Usage.title: Usage

UsageOut.description: The signed-in user's token quota, as it stands now (FR-12.5). Read only until S4.
UsageOut.title: UsageOut

UsageTotals.description: Sum of usage across a turn's model calls.

charged_tokens.description: What the turn took from the quota.
charged_tokens.title: Charged Tokens

UsageTotals.title: UsageTotals

info.description: Chat-first personal memory. The web app is one client of this API.
info.title: 2nd Mind API

get.description: Database (schema at head, app role under RLS), Redis, and provider config.

post.description:
Create or reuse the dev user (or the one named in the body) and their private workspace;
set the session cookie.

Write the recall fixture into the user's private workspace, once (a second call finds
it there and does nothing).
Apply a held write as a new turn (with its own diff, so undo still works).

patch.description:
Edit one memory in place, as its own turn (source ``ui_edit``) through the writer and
policy, with its own glass box; undo reverses it (FR-10.3). A date is free text read by
the resolver ("Friday", "3 October"); a delete is held for confirmation.

get.description:
The signed-in user's token quota: tier, limit, used and remaining (FR-12.5).
Read only: enforcement arrives in S4.
Build, routing and config hash this process runs with (FR-19.2).
The turn's structured events, in order: the glass box's source of truth (FR-9.2).

post.description:
Revert every memory write the turn made, as a new turn with its own diff (FR-10.1).
Undoing an undo turn is a redo.

get.description: Conversation history for a workspace, newest first (FR-1.6).

post.description: Send a message; the reply streams back as server-sent events.

200.description: A `text/event-stream` of frames: `turn.started`, then `token`, `step.started` and `turn.event` (each repeated, in the order they happened), then exactly one of `turn.completed` or `turn.failed`. Comment lines are keep-alives. Clients may ignore `step.started` and `turn.event`.

get.description:
Plans (with routine occurrences), reminders, tasks due and dated intentions in the next
``days`` (default ``UPCOMING_DAYS``), grouped by local day, plus undated open tasks
(S3.14). Built on the recall timeline tool.
